mcqs.question: What is the definition of work done by a constant force?

options.A: The product of the component of the force along the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement
options.B: The product of mass and acceleration

mcqs.answer: The product of the component of the force along the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as the scalar product of a constant force and the displacement in the direction of the force, i.e., W = F·s·cosθ. Option A states this definition correctly. Options B, C and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: The work done by a constant force \(F\) acting at an angle \(\theta\) to the displacement \(s\) is given by which expression?
mcqs.explanation: For a constant force, work is the dot product of force and displacement: \(W = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{s} = Fs\cos\theta\). Option A matches this formula. The other options use incorrect trigonometric functions or algebraic forms.

mcqs.question: When does a force do positive work on an object?

options.A: When the component of the force is in the same direction as the displacement
options.B: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement
options.C: When the force opposes the direction of displacement

mcqs.answer: When the component of the force is in the same direction as the displacement
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the force component along the displacement has the same direction as the displacement, giving a positive scalar value. Option A describes this situation. Perpendicular forces give zero work (B), opposite direction gives negative work (C), and no displacement yields zero work (D).

mcqs.question: A box is lifted upward while gravity acts downward. What is the work done by the gravitational force on the box?

options.A: Negative, because gravity opposes the upward displacement
options.B: Positive, because gravity is a force
options.D: It depends on the speed of lifting

mcqs.answer: Negative, because gravity opposes the upward displacement
mcqs.explanation: Gravity acts opposite to the upward displacement, so the angle between force and displacement is 180°, making \(\cos180° = -1\). Hence the work is negative. Option A captures this. Options B and C ignore the direction, and D is irrelevant to the sign of work.

mcqs.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit while the gravitational force always points toward the centre. What is the work done by gravity during one complete orbit?

options.A: Zero, because the force is always perpendicular to the displacement
options.B: Positive, because gravity is doing work
options.C: Negative, because the satellite is moving away from the force direction
options.D: Cannot be determined without the satellite’s speed

mcqs.answer: Zero, because the force is always perpendicular to the displacement
mcqs.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the displacement at any instant is tangential, while gravity is radial; the angle between them is 90°, making \(\cos90° = 0\). Therefore the work done over any segment, and hence over a full orbit, is zero. Option A states this correctly.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand work as a scalar quantity
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of work?

options.A: Work is a scalar quantity having only magnitude
options.B: Work is a vector quantity having both magnitude and direction
options.C: Work is a pseudo‑scalar that changes sign under inversion

mcqs.answer: Work is a scalar quantity having only magnitude
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as the dot product of two vectors, resulting in a scalar. It has magnitude (in joules) but no direction. Hence option A is correct. Options B, C, and D incorrectly assign vector, pseudo‑scalar, or tensor nature to work.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about work is incorrect?

options.A: Work can be done even if there is no displacement of the object
options.B: If the displacement is zero, the work done is zero
options.C: Work is a scalar quantity measured in joules
options.D: Work is the product of the component of force along displacement and the displacement

mcqs.answer: Work can be done even if there is no displacement of the object
mcqs.explanation: Work requires a displacement; if the object does not move, the work done is zero. Therefore statement A is false and is the correct answer to the question. Statements B, C, and D correctly describe work.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A constant force of 10 N acts on a block making an angle of 60° with the direction of a 5 m displacement. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work = F s cosθ = 10 N × 5 m × cos60° = 50 × 0.5 = 25 J. Option A gives the correct value. Option B ignores the cosine factor, option C uses sin60°, and option D would correspond to a perpendicular force, which is not the case here.
